paraphrases.question: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

items.stimulus: No reptile has fur. Every animal in this cage has fur.
items.question: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.text: No animal in this cage is a reptile.
Every furry animal is in this cage.
Some animals in this cage are mammals.
Reptiles cannot survive in cages.
The cage contains at least one snake.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: C could be true, but 'has fur' doesn't force any animal to be a mammal; only that none is a reptile is guaranteed (A).

paraphrases.stimulus: No plant can walk. Everything in this pen can walk.
paraphrases.question: If the statements are true, which one must also be true?

paraphrases.stimulus: No coin is made of paper. Every item in this drawer is made of paper.
paraphrases.question: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

items.stimulus: Every winter the town's only bridge freezes over and is closed for several days. The town's hospital sits on the far side of that bridge from where most residents live.
items.question: The statements above most strongly support which one of the following?

choices.text: In some winters, most residents may have trouble reaching the hospital for several days.
The town should build a second bridge across the river.
The hospital mostly treats injuries that occur in winter.
Most residents of the town never need the hospital.
The bridge freezes because it was poorly constructed.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: B recommends an action rather than stating what the facts support; the closure plus the hospital's location supports difficulty reaching it (A).

paraphrases.stimulus: Each spring the mountain road floods and closes for days. The village's only pharmacy sits beyond that road.
paraphrases.question: The statements above most strongly support which one of the following?

paraphrases.stimulus: Every storm season the ferry stops running for days. The island's only clinic can be reached only by that ferry.
paraphrases.question: The statements above most strongly support which one of the following?

items.stimulus: Workers who took a short midday walk reported sharper focus in the afternoon than those who did not. The company concluded that the walks improve focus.
items.question: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.text: When the non-walkers later began taking midday walks, their afternoon focus improved as well.
Most workers say they enjoy taking a midday walk.
The walking path around the office is well maintained.
Afternoon focus is difficult to measure precisely.
The company should require all workers to walk at midday.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: B merely restates that walks are pleasant; the before-and-after gain among former non-walkers (A) ties the walks to the improvement, supporting causation.

paraphrases.stimulus: Gardens given the new fertilizer grew taller plants than those without it, so the gardeners concluded the fertilizer causes taller growth.
paraphrases.question: Which one, if true, most strengthens the argument?

paraphrases.stimulus: Classes that used the new app scored higher than those that did not, so the school concluded the app raises scores.
paraphrases.question: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

items.stimulus: Neighborhoods with more streetlights have less crime. So installing more streetlights reduces crime.
items.question: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.text: Cities tend to install extra streetlights in neighborhoods that already have low crime.
Streetlights use only a small amount of electricity.
Some well-lit streets still experience occasional crime.
Streetlights make it easier to read street signs at night.
The city plans to install more streetlights next year.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: Occasional exceptions (C) are too weak; A reverses the causal story — low crime may prompt the lighting, not the other way around.

paraphrases.stimulus: Offices with more windows have happier staff, so adding windows must make staff happier.
paraphrases.question: Which one, if true, most weakens the argument?

paraphrases.stimulus: Schools with more counselors have fewer dropouts, so hiring counselors must reduce dropouts.
paraphrases.question: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

items.stimulus: Some say tablets should replace textbooks in every class. But a tablet's battery can die in the middle of a lesson, while a printed book never does. So we should not replace textbooks with tablets.
items.question: The argument proceeds by

choices.text: pointing out a practical drawback of a proposal in order to reject it.
attacking the character of those who favor tablets.
citing a study of student performance with each medium.
showing that the proposal contradicts itself.
offering a compromise that keeps some textbooks and some tablets.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The proposal isn't shown to be self-contradictory; the argument raises a practical disadvantage (a dead battery) to reject it (A).

paraphrases.stimulus: Some say email should replace all paper mail. But email can be lost to a server crash, while a letter cannot. So we should not replace paper mail with email.
paraphrases.question: The argument proceeds by

paraphrases.stimulus: Some argue we should pay only through a phone app. But a phone can run out of charge, while cash cannot. So we should not switch entirely to app payments.
paraphrases.question: The argument proceeds by

items.stimulus: Some people think we should cancel the school play to save money. But the play teaches teamwork and confidence, and ticket sales cover most of its cost. The school should keep the play.
items.question: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.text: The school should keep the play.
The play teaches teamwork and confidence.
The school play should be canceled to save money.
Ticket sales cover most of the play's cost.
Saving money is of no importance to the school.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: C is the opposing view the author argues against; the author's own conclusion is that the school should keep the play (A).

paraphrases.stimulus: Some want to close the community pool to cut costs. But the pool keeps children active and its fees pay for upkeep. The town should keep the pool open.
paraphrases.question: Which one most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

paraphrases.stimulus: A few argue for ending the free bus route to save money. But the route helps seniors shop and riders' fares cover much of it. The city should keep the route.
paraphrases.question: Which one most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

items.stimulus: All members of the choir can read music. Elena is a member of the choir. So Elena can read music.
items.question: Which one of the following exhibits reasoning most similar to that in the argument above?

choices.text: Every book in the series is a mystery. This is a book in the series. So it is a mystery.
Most athletes eat well, and Raj eats well, so Raj is probably an athlete.
All roses are flowers, so some flowers are roses.
If a shape is a square, it has four sides. This shape has four sides, so it is a square.
Some singers can read music, and Elena is a singer, so Elena can read music.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: E uses 'some', which cannot guarantee Elena reads music; the original and A both apply a universal ('all') to a member of the group (A).

paraphrases.stimulus: Every employee at the firm has a badge. Marta is an employee at the firm. So Marta has a badge.
paraphrases.question: Which one exhibits reasoning most similar to the argument above?

paraphrases.stimulus: All the trees in this orchard bear apples. This is a tree in the orchard. So it bears apples.
paraphrases.question: Which one of the following is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

items.stimulus: The rooster crows, and then the sun rises. So the rooster's crowing causes the sun to rise.
items.question: Which one of the following exhibits flawed reasoning most similar to that in the argument above?

choices.text: The streetlights switch on, and then it gets dark. So the streetlights cause the darkness.
Whenever it rains the ground gets wet; the ground is wet, so it must have rained.
Every time the team wins, fans cheer; fans are cheering, so the team won.
The kettle whistles because the water in it has boiled.
Since all clocks tick, this device that ticks must be a clock.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: B affirms the consequent (a different error); A copies the post hoc pattern exactly — one event follows another, so the first is said to cause the second.

paraphrases.stimulus: Every morning the newspaper arrives, and then traffic builds up, so the newspaper's arrival must cause the traffic.
paraphrases.question: Which one is most similar in its flawed reasoning to the argument above?

paraphrases.stimulus: The store opens, and shortly afterward crowds appear, so opening the store must cause the crowds to form.
paraphrases.question: Which one exhibits flawed reasoning most similar to that above?

items.passage: For years, city planners assumed that widening roads would ease traffic. Newer studies find the opposite: added lanes invite more drivers, so congestion soon returns. Some officials resist this finding, noting that a few widened highways did stay clear. The author argues that those exceptions usually had new train lines nearby, which drew traffic away, so the general pattern still holds.
items.question: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main point of the passage?

choices.text: Widening roads generally fails to relieve congestion, and the apparent exceptions have special explanations.
Building train lines is the only way to reduce traffic.
City planners have never studied traffic carefully.
Widening a highway always makes its congestion worse immediately.
Officials have shown that added lanes keep highways permanently clear.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The author says congestion 'soon returns', not that widening instantly worsens it; A captures the balanced main point, including the explained exceptions.

paraphrases.stimulus: Educators long believed that assigning more homework raised achievement. Recent research suggests the reverse: excess homework causes burnout and scores stall. Some teachers point to classes where heavy homework coincided with high scores, but the author notes those classes were also unusually small, which did the real work, so the overall pattern stands.
paraphrases.question: Which one most accurately expresses the main point of the passage?

paraphrases.stimulus: Managers assumed that longer hours boost output. Newer data show the opposite: fatigue lowers productivity over time. A few teams that worked long hours stayed productive, but the author observes they had just adopted new tools, which explained the gain, so the general trend holds.
paraphrases.question: Which one most accurately expresses the main point of the passage?

items.passage: The naturalist Maria Sibylla Merian traveled to South America in 1699 to study insects firsthand. At the time, most European scholars described exotic species only from dried specimens shipped home. Merian instead drew live insects alongside the specific plants they fed on, recording how each stage of life connected to its habitat. Her illustrations were dismissed by some as merely decorative, yet later biologists prized them precisely for the ecological relationships they preserved.
items.question: The passage most strongly supports which one of the following?

choices.text: Merian's method captured information that study of dried specimens alone would likely have missed.
European scholars of the time refused to study insects at all.
Merian was the first person ever to draw insects.
Dried specimens are useless for scientific work.
Later biologists considered Merian's illustrations purely decorative.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: E reverses the passage — later biologists prized the work for its ecological content; A follows from her drawing live insects with their host plants and life stages.

paraphrases.stimulus: The mapmaker Aiko Tanaka sailed the coast in person to chart its reefs, while most cartographers of her day copied older maps in their offices. She recorded currents and hazards as sailors reported them in real time. Some critics called her charts cluttered, but later navigators valued them for exactly the local detail they preserved.
paraphrases.question: The passage most supports which one of the following?

paraphrases.stimulus: The chef Amara Okoye visited farms to taste crops at harvest, whereas most food writers of her time judged ingredients only from market samples. She noted how soil and weather shaped each flavor. Some editors found her notes excessive, yet later cooks prized them for the growing conditions they captured.
paraphrases.question: The passage most strongly supports which one of the following?

items.passage: The public library began lending tools last year: drills, ladders, and garden equipment. Borrowers pay nothing and may keep each tool for a week. Staff say the program has proved popular, and very few tools have been damaged. The head librarian now hopes to add sewing machines to the collection.
items.question: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main point of the passage?

choices.text: The library has started a popular free tool-lending program and hopes to expand it.
Libraries should stop lending books to patrons.
Tools are more valuable to a community than books are.
The lending program has damaged a great many tools.
Sewing machines are the item patrons request most often.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The passage says few tools were damaged, the opposite of D; A states the program's success and the plan to expand it, which is the main point.

items.passage: (see rc-0104)

choices.text: provide evidence that the program has been working well.
warn that the program is beginning to fail.
explain why the library charges a borrowing fee.
criticize borrowers for being careless with tools.
argue that sewing machines should not be added.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: 'Few damaged' is offered as a success, not a warning; B reverses its function, while A matches the supportive point the detail makes.

items.passage: (see rc-0104)
items.question: The author's attitude toward the tool-lending program is best described as

choices.text: generally favorable.
sharply critical.
completely indifferent.
deeply alarmed.
openly regretful.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The author reports the program's popularity and low damage approvingly, so 'indifferent' misses the positive tone that A captures.

items.passage: (see rc-0104)

Sewing machines are already available for patrons to borrow.
Most borrowers end up damaging the tools they take home.
The program will certainly be canceled within a year.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The librarian only hopes to add sewing machines, so C overstates; the passage's 'borrowers pay nothing' directly supports free use of a drill (A).

items.passage: When the museum proposed charging admission, reactions split. Longtime members argued that free entry was central to the museum's mission of reaching everyone. The finance office countered that ticket revenue was needed to repair the aging roof. The director then proposed a middle path: keep entry free one day a week while charging on the other days.
items.question: The passage attributes which one of the following views to the longtime members?

Ticket revenue is needed to repair the roof.
Entry should be free only one day each week.
The museum should close entirely during repairs.
Admission should be charged every day of the week.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: B is the finance office's view, not the members'; the longtime members defend free entry as central to the mission (A).

items.passage: (see rc-0105)
items.question: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main point of the passage?

choices.text: Facing competing concerns about admission, the museum's director proposed a compromise.
The museum's aging roof cannot be repaired.
The longtime members have resigned from the museum.
Charging admission always reduces a museum's attendance.
The finance office controls all museum decisions.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The finance office only offers one argument, and the director decides; E overstates its role, while A captures the passage's overall arc toward a compromise.

items.passage: (see rc-0105)
items.question: Which one of the following best describes the organization of the passage?

choices.text: A proposal is made, two opposing concerns are presented, and a compromise is offered.
A single view is stated and then shown to be false.
A chronological history of the museum is provided.
A problem is posed and deliberately left unresolved.
Two unrelated topics are compared point by point.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The director's middle path resolves the dispute, so it isn't left open; A tracks the proposal / two-concerns / compromise structure.

items.stimulus: People who use the fitness app lose more weight than people who do not. So the app causes weight loss.
items.question: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.text: People who choose to use the app are already more committed to dieting than those who do not.
The fitness app is free to download.
Some users of the app lose only a little weight.
The app has a clean, pleasant design.
Losing weight tends to improve a person's health.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: A few small results (C) are too weak; A shows the users differ from non-users at the outset, so their commitment, not the app, may drive the loss.

items.stimulus: The mayor cut the ribbon on the new stadium, and attendance at city events rose that month. The ribbon-cutting must have boosted attendance.
items.question: The reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism because it

choices.text: concludes that one event caused another merely because it came first.
assumes the stadium was expensive to build.
concludes that attendance will keep rising forever.
ignores how popular the mayor already was.
restates that attendance rose that month.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The mayor's popularity (D) is one overlooked factor, but the core error is post hoc reasoning — treating 'came first' as 'caused it' (A).

items.stimulus: The store should stay open until midnight. Sales in the final hour before closing are always strong.
items.question: The argument depends on assuming which one of the following?

choices.text: At least some customers would make purchases between the current closing time and midnight.
The final hour is the store's single most profitable hour of the day.
The store currently closes earlier than all of its competitors.
Employees prefer working evenings to working mornings.
Late-night shoppers spend more per visit than daytime shoppers.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: B is too strong; the argument needs only that staying open later would bring some sales (A), not that the last hour beats every other hour.

items.stimulus: A radio host asked listeners to call in about the new law, and most callers opposed it. So most citizens oppose the new law.
items.question: The reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism because it

choices.text: relies on a self-selected group of callers who may not reflect citizens generally.
assumes the new law will eventually be repealed.
concludes that the new law is unconstitutional.
ignores the specific reasons the callers gave.
restates that most callers opposed the law.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: E notes a restatement, but the defect is generalizing from callers who chose to phone in — an unrepresentative sample (A).

items.stimulus: All the marbles in the bag are blue. Nothing blue is made of glass.
items.question: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.text: None of the marbles in the bag is made of glass.
Every blue object is a marble in the bag.
Some of the marbles in the bag are made of plastic.
The bag contains at least one marble.
Blue is the most common color for marbles.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: C could be true, but the premises don't fix any marble's material beyond 'not glass'; only that none is glass is guaranteed (A).

items.stimulus: Passing the road test is required to get a driver's license. Priya passed the road test, so she will get a license.
items.question: The reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism because it

choices.text: treats passing the road test, which is only one requirement, as though it were enough for a license.
assumes that Priya wants a driver's license.
concludes that everyone who passes the road test drives well.
ignores how long Priya practiced driving.
restates that the road test is required.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: E restates a premise; the flaw is treating a necessary condition (the road test) as if it were sufficient for the license (A).

items.stimulus: The new library branch will be heavily used. It is being built in the neighborhood that has the most families with young children.
items.question: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.text: Families with young children use library branches more than any other group does.
The new branch will include a large parking lot.
The same neighborhood already contains several busy bookstores.
Library branches are costly for a city to operate.
The city already operates many library branches.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: Nearby bookstores (C) would compete for readers, if anything weakening the claim; A ties young families to heavy library use, supporting it.

items.stimulus: A higher percentage of flights were delayed at the small regional airport than at the massive international hub. So the regional airport delayed more flights than the hub did.
items.question: The reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism because it

choices.text: confuses a higher proportion of delays with a greater number of delayed flights.
assumes that all flight delays last the same amount of time.
concludes that the regional airport is poorly managed.
ignores the causes of the flight delays.
restates that the delay percentage was higher at the regional airport.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: E flags a restatement, but the decisive error is inferring a larger count from a larger percentage (A) — the hub handles far more flights.

items.stimulus: Critics claim the city's new bus lanes slow down cars. In fact, car travel times have barely changed, while buses now run far faster. The bus lanes have been a success.
items.question: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.text: The city's new bus lanes have been a success.
The bus lanes slow down car traffic.
Buses now run faster than they did before.
Car travel times have barely changed.
Cars should be banned from the city center entirely.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: B is the critics' claim the author rebuts; the author's own conclusion is that the bus lanes have been a success (A).

items.stimulus: We must either build the new dam or accept frequent flooding. Since no one wants frequent flooding, we have to build the dam.
items.question: The reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism because it

choices.text: assumes that only two options exist when other flood-control measures may be possible.
assumes that the dam will never fail.
concludes that flooding is impossible to survive.
ignores the cost of building the dam.
restates that no one wants frequent flooding.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: E notes a restatement, but the flaw is the false either/or; levees or other measures could also prevent flooding (A).

items.stimulus: Every loaf of bread this bakery sells is baked the same morning it is sold. The cafe next door buys all of its bread from this bakery.
items.question: The statements above most strongly support which one of the following?

choices.text: The bread the cafe serves was baked that same morning.
The cafe bakes its own bread fresh each morning.
The bakery sells only bread and no pastries.
The cafe is the bakery's single largest customer.
Freshly baked bread tastes better than day-old bread.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: D could be true but isn't supported — buying all its bread there says nothing about size relative to other customers; that the cafe's bread is same-morning (A) follows directly.

items.stimulus: The senator's plan to expand the city's parks deserves no consideration. After all, the senator has been divorced twice.
items.question: The reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism because it

choices.text: dismisses a proposal by pointing to an irrelevant fact about the person who made it.
assumes that the parks plan would be too expensive.
concludes that the senator will lose the next election.
ignores the likely benefits of expanding the parks.
restates that the senator has been divorced twice.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: Overlooking benefits (D) isn't the core defect; the flaw is rejecting the plan by attacking the senator's personal life instead of the plan itself (A).

items.stimulus: This year the museum sold more memberships than ever before, yet its total attendance fell compared with last year.
items.question: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy?

choices.text: Last year a hugely popular traveling exhibit drew large one-time crowds who did not return this year.
Memberships cost slightly more this year than they did last year.
The museum opened two new galleries this year.
Members receive a discount at the museum gift shop.
Attendance is counted by scanning tickets at the front door.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: New galleries (C) would tend to raise attendance, deepening the puzzle; only the loss of last year's exhibit crowds (A) explains why total attendance fell despite more members.

items.stimulus: Neighborhoods with more ice cream shops report more sunburns. So the ice cream shops must be causing the sunburns.
items.question: The reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism because it

choices.text: overlooks that hot, sunny weather could independently increase both ice cream sales and sunburns.
assumes that everyone in the neighborhood eats ice cream.
concludes that ice cream is bad for one's health.
ignores the price of ice cream in each neighborhood.
restates that shops and sunburns occur together.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: E notes the correlation restated, but the flaw is ignoring a common cause — sunny weather — that drives both variables (A).

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who regularly drink energy drinks tend to have higher grades than those who do not. Therefore, drinking energy drinks must improve academic performance.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument above?

choices.text: Many students who drink energy drinks also study more hours, which contributes to their higher grades.
Energy drinks are popular among students in high-performing schools.
The consumption of energy drinks has doubled in the past five years among high school students.
Students who drink energy drinks often report feeling more awake and alert during classes.
Most students believe that energy drinks help them focus better on their studies.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it discusses the popularity of energy drinks in successful schools, it does not address the relationship between energy drink consumption and academic performance.

items.stimulus: Recently, a study found that students who regularly participate in after-school clubs tend to have higher grades than those who do not. Furthermore, these students reported that being in clubs helps them develop better time management skills and increases their motivation to study.
items.question: Which of the following must be true based on the study's findings?

choices.text: Students who participate in after-school clubs likely develop better time management skills.
All students who join after-school clubs will achieve higher grades than those who do not.
After-school clubs have no impact on students' grades or motivation.
Motivated students are more likely to join after-school clubs.

items.question: What role does the claim about studies showing regular exercise improves mental health play in the argument?

choices.text: It supports the conclusion that increasing physical activity will enhance mental well-being.
It provides an alternative explanation for why mental health may improve in certain people.
It assumes that mental well-being is solely dependent on physical activity levels.
It presents a counterargument against the benefits of exercise for mental health.
It reinforces the idea that mental health treatment should solely focus on physical fitness.

items.stimulus: During a recent study, participants who consumed caffeine reported feeling more alert than those who did not consume caffeine. However, the study did not measure the participants' actual performance on tasks that require alertness.

choices.text: Caffeine consumption is associated with a subjective increase in alertness.
Caffeine consumption improves task performance in all individuals.
Non-caffeine consumers feel less alert than caffeine consumers in every situation.

The developer should consider using traditional roofing materials to save costs, since the policy is only a suggestion.
The developer should lobby against the policy because it imposes unnecessary restrictions on building designs.
The developer should include a plan for a rooftop garden that does not involve a green roof, as this would still benefit the environment.
The developer should build a building without a roof to maximize efficiency, as roofs do not significantly impact building performance.

Late-night studying has become increasingly common among students in recent years.

items.stimulus: In a recent study, researchers found that students who study late at night scored higher on math tests compared to those who study in the morning. Therefore, studying at night is the best approach to improve math scores for all students.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: Choice B introduces a claim about citizen preferences, which is irrelevant to the argument's focus on the effect of bike lanes on traffic congestion.

items.stimulus: During a recent survey of local businesses, it was found that 70% of owners believe that increasing online advertising leads to higher sales. Therefore, the city should invest in initiatives to help local businesses increase their online advertising, since this will boost the city’s overall economic growth.
items.question: Which of the following is a necessary assumption for the conclusion drawn above to be true?

choices.text: Increasing online advertising is a significant factor in driving economic growth for the city.
All local businesses have the resources necessary to increase their online advertising without financial strain.
The survey accurately represents the views of all local businesses in the city.
Higher sales for local businesses will lead to an increase in job opportunities within the city.
Online advertising is more effective than traditional advertising methods for local businesses.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it may seem relevant, the ability of businesses to increase advertising is not necessary for the conclusion about boosting the city’s economic growth to hold.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that cities with more parks have lower rates of anxiety among their residents. Therefore, increasing the number of parks in a city will likely reduce anxiety levels among its inhabitants.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument that increasing parks causes a reduction in anxiety levels?

choices.text: Residents of cities that have added parks report lower anxiety levels compared to before the parks were added.
Many factors contribute to anxiety levels in residents, including employment status and social support.
Parks in cities often attract more visitors, leading to increased happiness among those visitors.
Cities with lower anxiety levels tend to have larger populations of young families.
Some cities have more funding for mental health services than others, which correlates with lower anxiety rates.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While B mentions other factors affecting anxiety, it does not support the specific relationship between parks and anxiety reduction.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who study late at night score higher on math tests than those who study in the morning. Therefore, studying late at night causes students to perform better on math tests.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument above?

choices.text: Students who study late at night are far more likely than students who study in the morning to receive private math tutoring, which on its own raises math test scores.
Students who study late at night report enjoying their study sessions more than students who study in the morning do.
The math test scores of students who study in the morning have risen over the past few years as those students adopted new study techniques.
Students who study late at night often say they feel more alert during those hours.
Many students prefer studying in the morning because they believe it helps them retain information better than studying at night.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: Enjoying late-night sessions is merely a correlate of studying late; it supplies no alternative cause for the higher math scores, so it does not undermine the causal claim.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who study late at night score higher on math tests than those who study in the morning. Therefore, if students want to improve their math scores, they should consider studying late at night.
items.question: Which of the following is a necessary assumption for the conclusion to be valid?

choices.text: Studying late at night is more effective for improving math scores than studying in the morning.
All students have the same capacity for improvement regardless of their study habits.
Math is the only subject that benefits from late-night studying.
The study accounted for other factors that might influence math scores, such as prior knowledge or study methods.
Students who study late at night are generally less attentive than those who study in the morning.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: This choice assumes uniformity among students that is not established by the argument, thus it does not directly support the conclusion about studying late at night.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who regularly study in the evening score higher on math tests than those who study in the morning. Therefore, if we want to improve students' math scores, we should encourage them to study in the evening rather than in the morning.
items.question: What assumption is necessary for the conclusion to be true?

choices.text: Evening study habits directly lead to improved math scores, rather than other factors influencing both study time and test performance.
Students who score higher on math tests also study longer hours regardless of the time they study.
Students prefer studying in the evening over the morning, making it a more effective time for studying.
Morning study is ineffective for all subjects, not just math.
The study's findings apply to all students, regardless of their individual circumstances or learning styles.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While longer study hours may seem relevant, the argument specifically focuses on the timing of study, not the duration.

items.stimulus: The city council has decided to donate surplus food from local restaurants to shelters. This decision is based on the principle that helping those in need is a community responsibility, and that food waste should be minimized whenever possible.
items.question: According to the principle on which the city council based its decision, which of the following actions would also be consistent with that principle?

choices.text: Creating a community garden to provide fresh produce to low-income families.
Organizing a food festival to promote local restaurants and increase their profits.
Implementing a tax break for restaurants that renovate their dining rooms to attract more paying customers.
Encouraging grocery stores to throw away expired goods rather than donating them.
Funding an advertising campaign for local farmers to sell their goods directly to consumers.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While promoting local restaurants may seem beneficial, it aims at profit and does not address the principle of helping those in need or minimizing food waste.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that people who regularly consume green tea have a lower risk of developing heart disease compared to those who do not. Therefore, drinking green tea can help prevent heart disease in the general population.
items.question: Which of the following is a necessary assumption for the argument to hold?

choices.text: Regular green tea consumers are representative of the general population in terms of heart disease risk factors.
All beverages consumed by green tea drinkers do not have negative effects on heart health.
Drinking green tea has a stronger impact on heart disease prevention than other lifestyle factors, such as diet or exercise.
People who drink green tea are more likely to seek medical advice than those who do not.
The study's results can be generalized to all types of tea consumption.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The argument does not require that all beverages consumed by green tea drinkers are harmless, only that their consumption of green tea correlates with lower heart disease risk.

items.stimulus: A recent study conducted on a small group of 30 college students concluded that most college students prefer online classes over traditional in-person classes. Given this finding, the researchers recommend that all universities shift their focus towards offering more online classes, as this preference is likely universal among all college students.
items.question: What is the flaw in the researchers' reasoning?

choices.text: The conclusion is based on a sample that is too small and not representative of the entire population of college students.
The researchers assume that online classes are inherently better than traditional classes without considering other factors.
The study does not account for the specific preferences of students in different majors, which may vary significantly.
The researchers fail to recognize that student preferences can change over time, making their conclusion unsustainable.
The statement ignores the potential benefits of in-person classes that some students might still prefer.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: This choice misinterprets the argument by suggesting the researchers are asserting that online classes are better, rather than focusing on the flawed sample leading to their conclusion.

items.stimulus: During the winter months, people tend to wear heavier clothing to stay warm. Therefore, in cold weather, wearing heavier clothing is the best way to keep comfortable.
items.question: What general principle underlies the argument in the statement above?

choices.text: Wearing appropriate clothing for the weather can lead to comfort.
Heavier clothing is the only way to stay warm in winter.
People are uncomfortable in cold weather.
Comfort is solely determined by the weight of clothing.
Wearing lighter clothing in winter is just as effective as heavier clothing.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While heavier clothing helps with warmth, saying it's the only way to stay warm is too strong a claim.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that people who regularly play video games tend to have better hand-eye coordination than those who do not. The study did not explore whether this improved coordination translates to other real-world skills, such as driving or playing sports.
items.question: Which of the following is most strongly supported by the study's findings?

choices.text: Regular video game players likely have superior hand-eye coordination compared to non-players.
All activities that require hand-eye coordination are improved by playing video games.
Playing video games may help improve driving skills due to better hand-eye coordination.
There is no correlation between video game playing and athletic performance.
People who don’t play video games are at a disadvantage in activities requiring coordination.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it's tempting to think video games improve all coordination-related activities, the study doesn't support this broad claim.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that people who frequently consume fast food tend to have lower overall health scores compared to those who do not. Therefore, it must be true that avoiding fast food leads to better health outcomes.
items.question: Which of the following assumptions, if true, would guarantee that the conclusion is valid?

choices.text: People who avoid fast food are more likely to engage in other healthy behaviors that contribute to better health outcomes.
Eating fast food is the only factor affecting health scores among the study participants.
All individuals in the study who consumed fast food reported lower health scores regardless of their age or activity levels.
Many people believe that fast food is unhealthy, which may influence their food choices.
The study involved a diverse group of participants with varying health backgrounds.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: This choice attributes better health to other behaviors rather than to avoiding fast food; far from guaranteeing the conclusion, it undermines it by supplying an alternative cause.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that people who drink green tea regularly have lower cholesterol levels than those who do not drink green tea. Therefore, drinking green tea must lead to lower cholesterol levels.
items.question: Which of the following is an assumption that, if added, would guarantee the conclusion?

choices.text: The people in the study did not have other significant lifestyle factors that could affect cholesterol levels.
All types of tea have health benefits that affect cholesterol levels.
Drinking green tea is the only way to lower cholesterol levels.
Lower cholesterol levels are the most important health marker for overall health.
The participants in the study were all adults aged 30 to 50.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: This choice asserts a broad claim about all types of tea, which is irrelevant to the specific case of green tea and does not support the conclusion.

items.stimulus: Despite being a highly rated restaurant known for its delicious dishes, Bistro Gourmet recently reported a significant decline in customer visits. However, local food critics have praised the restaurant's quality in their reviews, noting that the chef's innovative menu is still impressive. This presents an apparent contradiction: how can a restaurant with excellent reviews experience a drop in clientele?
items.question: Which of the following, if true, helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy between Bistro Gourmet's high ratings and its declining customer visits?

choices.text: Bistro Gourmet increased its prices recently, causing some regular customers to seek more affordable alternatives.
Many people prefer to eat at home after the recent rise in food delivery options.
Bistro Gourmet hasn't changed its menu in over a year, leading to customer dissatisfaction despite high ratings.
Local food critics have a history of favoring well-presented dishes over taste when rating restaurants.
Bistro Gourmet has been featured on social media platforms, increasing its visibility despite the decline in visits.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it suggests a general trend that might affect customer behavior, it doesn't directly explain the specific situation of Bistro Gourmet.

items.stimulus: Researchers have found a strong correlation between the number of hours students spend studying and their scores on standardized tests. Based on this correlation, they conclude that increasing study hours will lead to higher test scores for all students.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the researchers' conclusion?

choices.text: Some students who study for more hours do not perform well on tests because they struggle with test anxiety, which is unrelated to study time.
Many students report that they study fewer hours than they would like but still achieve high scores.
The quality of study time, such as engaging in effective study techniques, is more important than the quantity of hours studied.
Students who study less than the average amount are more likely to seek help and tutoring, thus improving their test scores.
Test scores have increased overall in recent years, regardless of study hours, due to better teaching methods.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While this choice discusses student performance, it does not address the causal relationship implied between study hours and scores.

items.stimulus: A new study has shown that students who study in groups perform better on math tests than those who study alone. Therefore, implementing group study sessions in all math classes will improve overall math scores for all students.
items.question: Which one of the following assumptions, if true, would guarantee that the implementation of group study sessions will improve overall math scores for all students?

choices.text: Every student in these math classes will take part in the group study sessions, and studying in a group raises the math score of any student who does so.
All students find group study sessions enjoyable and advantageous for their learning.
The group study sessions will be structured in a way that promotes effective collaboration among students.
Math scores are primarily determined by study habits and not by factors like teacher effectiveness.
Students who perform better on math tests are more likely to continue studying math in the future.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: That students enjoy and value the sessions neither ensures every student participates nor guarantees that participation actually raises scores, so it cannot make the conclusion follow.

items.stimulus: The city's new recycling program has dramatically increased the amount of materials being recycled. Therefore, the program is clearly successful in promoting environmental sustainability.
items.question: What assumption must be true for the conclusion to be valid?

choices.text: The increased recycling will lead to a measurable improvement in environmental health.
Most city residents are participating in the recycling program.
The program is the only factor influencing recycling rates in the city.
Environmental sustainability is solely determined by recycling rates.
Other cities with similar programs have also seen increases in recycling rates.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While resident participation might contribute to the program's perceived success, it does not address the necessary link between recycling and overall environmental sustainability.

items.stimulus: During a recent city council meeting, several residents expressed concerns about the increase in traffic congestion due to new housing developments. In response, the mayor stated that more housing is essential for attracting new businesses and boosting the local economy. Therefore, the mayor concluded that the traffic congestion caused by these developments should not be a major concern.
items.question: What is the main conclusion of the mayor's argument?

choices.text: The benefits of new housing developments outweigh the traffic congestion they cause.
Traffic congestion is a significant issue that needs more attention from the city council.
Attracting new businesses is important for the local economy.
The city council should prioritize traffic reduction over housing development.
Residents are generally opposed to any new housing developments.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it acknowledges an issue, it does not reflect the mayor's conclusion that traffic congestion should not be a major concern.

items.stimulus: A recent study showed that students who participate in after-school tutoring programs tend to improve their grades significantly compared to those who do not. Therefore, schools should implement after-school tutoring programs to help all students achieve better academic outcomes.
items.question: Which of the following arguments is most similar in logical structure to the argument above?

choices.text: A survey found that people who regularly exercise have lower stress levels than those who do not. Consequently, workplaces should offer gym memberships to reduce employee stress.
Research indicates that eating breakfast can lead to better concentration in class. However, not all students who skip breakfast will perform poorly in school.

A new health initiative showed that individuals who quit smoking experience improved lung function. Thus, quitting smoking is beneficial for health regardless of the individual's current health status.
An analysis found that households with pets tend to report higher levels of happiness. Therefore, having a pet will certainly make anyone happier, regardless of their situation.
A team of researchers concluded that students who participate in sports are more likely to develop teamwork skills. Thus, all students should join sports teams to gain these skills.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While B discusses the potential benefits of breakfast for concentration, it introduces an irrelevant qualification about performance that diverts from the core point of implementing a program for all.

items.stimulus: After observing a significant decrease in the number of customers at his cafe during the summer months, the owner concluded that outdoor seating is essential for attracting more customers. He believes that if he adds more outdoor seating, his sales will increase significantly, as summer is the perfect time for people to enjoy meals outside.
items.question: What is the main conclusion of the cafe owner's argument?

choices.text: Adding outdoor seating will increase summer sales at the cafe.
The cafe is losing customers because it lacks outdoor seating.
Summer is a busy time for cafes with outdoor seating.
Customers prefer eating outside during the summer months.
The cafe owner has observed changes in customer preferences over time.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it correctly identifies a reason for customer loss, it does not capture the owner's conclusion about adding outdoor seating as a solution.

items.stimulus: During the school board meeting, the principal stated that students who participate in extracurricular activities generally perform better academically than those who do not. Therefore, if we want to improve the overall academic performance of our students, we should encourage all students to join at least one extracurricular activity.
items.question: Which of the following assumptions, if true, would most strongly support the principal's conclusion?

choices.text: Participation in extracurricular activities directly contributes to improved academic skills.
All students have the resources and time to participate in extracurricular activities without negatively impacting their studies.
Only students who already excel academically choose to join extracurricular activities.
Extracurricular activities are equally effective in improving academic performance across different subjects.
Students who do poorly academically are generally uninterested in extracurricular activities.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it suggests feasibility, it does not guarantee that encouraging participation will improve academic performance.

items.stimulus: After a new study revealed that eating breakfast improves cognitive performance in children, several local schools decided to implement a free breakfast program. Teachers at these schools reported that students who participated in the breakfast program showed increased focus and participation in class compared to those who did not eat breakfast.
items.question: Which of the following can be inferred from the statements above?

choices.text: Students who eat breakfast are more likely to perform better in school-related tasks than those who do not eat breakfast.
The breakfast program is the only factor contributing to improved student performance in class.
All children perform better academically if they eat breakfast every day.
The study indicates that students in schools without breakfast programs are equally focused in class.
Teachers noticed no difference in participation among students who skipped breakfast and those who ate it.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The statement claims the breakfast program is the only factor influencing performance, while the stimulus only suggests a correlation, not causation.

items.stimulus: Last summer, the local park experienced a sudden increase in visitors after the new ice cream shop opened nearby. Therefore, the opening of the ice cream shop must have caused the increase in park visitors.
items.question: What is the flaw in the argument?

choices.text: It assumes that a correlation between two events implies that one event caused the other.
It overlooks other possible reasons why more people might visit the park, such as the warmer weather.
It relies too heavily on anecdotal evidence from just one summer season.
It suggests that all park visitors only go to the park for ice cream, which is an extreme assumption.
It incorrectly assumes that fewer visitors would have gone to the park without the ice cream shop.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While the argument does overlook other reasons for increased park visitors, the primary flaw involves assuming causation solely based on the timing of the events.

items.stimulus: Many local coffee shops have started offering discounts to customers who bring their own reusable cups. This initiative not only helps reduce waste but also encourages environmentally conscious behavior among customers. Therefore, promoting sustainable practices can lead to positive changes in consumer habits.
items.question: Which of the following principles underlies the argument above?

choices.text: Encouraging sustainable behaviors can lead to broader environmental benefits.
Discounts for reusable items are primarily effective for increasing revenue for businesses.
Consumers will only adopt sustainable practices if they receive financial incentives.
Most coffee shop customers are unaware of the environmental impact of disposable cups.
Reusing materials is less effective than recycling in reducing waste.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While discounts may affect some customer behavior, the principle of promoting sustainable practices encompasses more than just revenue implications.

items.stimulus: During a recent community festival, local vendors reported that their sales were significantly lower than expected, despite a higher than usual number of visitors. Many vendors expressed confusion about this discrepancy, as they had prepared extensively for the event, expecting that a larger crowd would lead to increased sales.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, could help explain the discrepancy between the higher number of visitors and the lower sales reported by vendors?

choices.text: Many visitors only attended the festival to enjoy the atmosphere and did not intend to purchase anything.
The festival featured a wider variety of food options this year than in previous years.
Vendors raised their prices significantly from the previous year, leading to fewer purchases.
A popular celebrity made an appearance at the festival, attracting more visitors than anticipated.
Several vendors ran out of their best-selling items early in the event.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The presence of more food options may not directly explain why sales were lower, as it does not address visitors' purchasing intentions.

items.stimulus: In a recent survey of coffee drinkers, 70% reported that they preferred dark roast over light roast. Furthermore, among those who preferred dark roast, 60% stated that they believed dark roast coffee has more flavor than light roast coffee. Meanwhile, only 30% of light roast drinkers thought light roasts were more flavorful than dark roasts. This suggests a strong preference for dark roast among the surveyed population, with a significant belief in its superior flavor.
items.question: Which of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices.text: A substantial portion of the coffee drinkers in the survey believe that dark roast coffee is more flavorful than light roast coffee.
All coffee drinkers prefer dark roast over light roast coffee, indicating that light roast coffee is unpopular.
Some dark roast coffee drinkers might actually prefer light roast coffee if given the choice.
A greater percentage of surveyed coffee drinkers believe that dark roast is less flavorful than light roast than believe the reverse.
There is no difference in flavor preference between dark roast and light roast coffee drinkers outside of this survey.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The statement claims 'all' coffee drinkers prefer dark roast, which is far stronger than the 70% figure the survey supports.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who study late at night tend to have higher grades than those who study in the morning. Therefore, studying late at night causes students to achieve higher grades.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument that studying late at night causes higher grades?

choices.text: Students who study at night report feeling more alert and focused during their study sessions than those who study in the morning.
Many students who study in the morning also achieve high grades, but this is less common.
The study did not account for whether the students engaged in extracurricular activities during the day.
Some students study late at night but still receive low grades.
The study included a diverse group of students from various backgrounds and disciplines.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: This choice suggests that studying in the morning can also lead to high grades, which does not support the conclusion that studying late at night is the cause of higher grades.

items.stimulus: Recent studies have shown that students who regularly engage in physical exercise tend to have higher academic performance than those who do not exercise. Therefore, incorporating physical exercise into the school curriculum will improve students' academic outcomes.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most seriously weaken the argument above?

choices.text: Many students who excel academically also participate in extracurricular activities that include physical exercise, suggesting that a third factor influences both exercise and academic success.
Schools that recently added physical exercise programs have not yet collected enough data to determine whether academic performance has changed.
A significant number of students who do not engage in physical exercise still perform well academically, indicating that physical exercise is not necessary for academic success.
Some educational experts argue that academic performance can be improved through better teaching methods rather than physical exercise.
Physical exercise has numerous health benefits for students, which could indirectly contribute to better academic performance.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: Reporting that there is not yet enough data on existing programs is inconclusive; it does not identify any flaw in the reasoning from correlation to causation.

items.stimulus: In a recent survey, 70% of participants reported that they prefer organic foods over non-organic foods. Therefore, it can be concluded that a majority of consumers in the general population prefer organic foods.
items.question: What assumption is necessary for the conclusion to hold?

choices.text: The survey participants represent a diverse cross-section of the general population.
All consumers are aware of the differences between organic and non-organic foods.
A majority of health experts also prefer organic foods over non-organic foods.
Organic foods are more popular than non-organic foods in all regions of the country.
Most consumers are willing to pay higher prices for organic foods.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: Whether consumers understand the differences is not required by the inference; the conclusion can hold even if some consumers are unaware, so negating it does not break the argument.

items.stimulus: The mayor of Springfield recently announced that the city should invest in a new sports complex, citing that many professional athletes endorse such facilities. Therefore, the new sports complex will undoubtedly bring economic benefits to the city.
items.question: Which of the following arguments contains a similar flaw to the mayor's argument?

choices.text: A celebrity chef claims that a new culinary school will increase the city's tourism, and therefore, local officials have decided to fund it based on her endorsement alone.
City planners argue that investing in public parks will improve community health, citing studies that show people who exercise outdoors are generally healthier.
The president of a tech company believes that the release of a new gadget will revolutionize the market, without referring to any sales data to support this claim.
A respected economist suggests that tax cuts lead to increased consumer spending because he feels it would make people happier, thus the government plans to implement them.
A local artist states that public murals can enhance community pride, so the city council decides to allocate funds for a mural project, citing previous successful projects as evidence.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While B discusses health benefits, it does so based on studies, not solely relying on an individual's endorsement.

items.stimulus: In recent studies, researchers found that plants which received more sunlight grew taller than those that received less. Thus, it can be concluded that to increase the height of houseplants, one should place them in a location with abundant sunlight.
items.question: Which of the following arguments has a reasoning structure most similar to the argument above?

choices.text: In an experiment, it was shown that children who read more books perform better in school than those who read fewer. Therefore, children should be encouraged to read more to improve their academic performance.
A survey indicated that people who exercise regularly feel healthier than those who do not. This suggests that feeling healthier is solely dependent on regular exercise.
An analysis revealed that students who study late at night tend to get lower grades than those who study in the morning. Thus, studying at night is detrimental to academic success.
Observations show that dogs that are walked daily are happier than those that are not walked often. This implies that simply having a dog will make someone happy.
Data suggests that people who consume less sugar have lower rates of obesity, but this does not necessarily mean reducing sugar intake will prevent obesity in all individuals.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While B discusses a correlation between exercise and health, it mistakenly implies a direct causation, which shifts the argument's focus.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who study late at night score higher on math tests than those who study in the morning. Therefore, if students want to improve their math scores, they should consider studying late at night.
items.question: Which of the following arguments has a structure similar to the argument above?

choices.text: A survey revealed that people who exercise regularly tend to report higher levels of happiness than those who do not exercise. Thus, to be happier, individuals should incorporate regular exercise into their routines.

Researchers have shown that children who read more books achieve better results in standardized tests compared to those who read fewer books. Thus, reading books will certainly help all children do better in school.

A recent trend suggests that students who attend classes online often find it easier to balance work and study. Therefore, online classes might not be the best choice if one prefers face-to-face interactions with professors.

A report indicated that people who drink coffee are generally more alert than those who do not. However, this does not imply that drinking coffee is necessary for everyone to stay awake during the day.

An analysis showed that individuals who eat breakfast regularly tend to feel more energetic throughout the day than those who skip breakfast. Therefore, skipping breakfast could lead to lower energy levels in some people.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While B follows a similar format, it makes an overgeneralization about reading books, which is not warranted by the study's results.

items.stimulus: During a recent study on workplace productivity, researchers found that employees who take regular breaks throughout the day report higher job satisfaction and improved focus. Consequently, management has decided to implement mandatory break periods for all staff.
items.question: Which of the following must be true based on the statements above?

choices.text: Implementing mandatory break periods is intended to enhance employee satisfaction.
Employees will become less productive during mandatory break periods.
Job satisfaction is the only factor that affects workplace productivity.
All employees desire more breaks than they currently take.
The decision to implement mandatory breaks is based solely on the findings of this study.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it may seem that breaks could lead to less productivity, the study indicates the opposite regarding overall employee satisfaction and focus.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who study later in the evening tend to have higher grades than those who study in the morning. Therefore, studying in the evening causes students to achieve better grades.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument above?

choices.text: Many students who study late also tend to participate in extracurricular activities that enhance their learning and grades.
Students who study at night are somewhat more likely to prefer staying up late, a personal habit that has no bearing on academic ability or grades.
There are no studies showing that morning studying is ineffective.
Students' grades are influenced by many factors such as teacher quality and parental involvement.
Some students find studying at night makes them more alert and focused than studying in the morning.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: This choice explicitly makes the late-night habit irrelevant to grades, so it identifies no alternative cause and leaves the timing-to-grades inference untouched.

items.stimulus: In a recent survey, 70% of dog owners reported that their pets help them feel less stressed. Additionally, 50% of these dog owners stated that they walk their dogs daily. Experts suggest that regular exercise, such as walking dogs, can significantly improve mental health and reduce anxiety levels.
items.question: Which of the following is most strongly supported by the statements above?

choices.text: Walking dogs may contribute to reducing stress for dog owners.
All dog owners experience reduced stress levels because of their pets.
Only those dog owners who walk their dogs feel less stressed.
Dog ownership is the sole factor that helps alleviate stress among individuals.

items.stimulus: Many people believe that exercising regularly leads to improved mental health. A recent study found that participants who engaged in regular physical activity reported higher levels of joy and lower levels of stress than those who did not exercise. Therefore, regular exercise is essential for maintaining good mental health.
items.question: Which of the following is an assumption required by the argument above?

choices.text: Improved mental health is associated with increased joy and decreased stress.
All forms of physical activity lead to the same mental health benefits.
People who do not exercise are generally unhappier than those who do not.
Only regular exercise can lead to improved mental health.
Mental health is determined solely by physical activities.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The argument does not require that all forms of physical activity provide the same benefits, just that exercising regularly is tied to improved mental health.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who participate in extracurricular activities tend to have higher GPAs than those who do not. Therefore, it is likely that participating in extracurricular activities causes students to achieve higher GPAs.
items.question: Which of the following is a necessary assumption made by the argument above?

choices.text: Students who have higher GPAs are not necessarily those who are simply more academically inclined, regardless of extracurricular participation.
All students who participate in extracurricular activities have higher GPAs than those who do not.
The study's findings apply to all types of extracurricular activities equally.
There are no other factors influencing the GPAs of the students studied.

items.stimulus: In a recent study, researchers found that students who study in groups perform better on exams than those who study alone. Some educators argue that promoting group study sessions could enhance overall student performance at schools. However, critics point out that group dynamics can sometimes hinder individual understanding, suggesting that group study may not always be beneficial.
items.question: What role does the statement about critics' concerns regarding group dynamics play in the argument?

choices.text: It introduces a counterargument to the claim that group study sessions enhance performance.
It provides evidence supporting the benefits of group study sessions.
It concludes that group study should be discouraged altogether.
It suggests that individual study is always superior to group study.
It implies that group study has no impact on individual performance.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it may seem like the critics are providing evidence against group study, their concerns actually serve as a counterpoint rather than directly supporting the initial claim about benefits.

items.stimulus: In a recent study, researchers found that students who study in groups perform better on tests than those who study alone. This suggests that collaborative learning environments enhance educational outcomes.
items.question: What general principle underlies the argument presented in the stimulus?

choices.text: Collaborative learning is generally more effective than solitary learning in improving academic performance.
Students should always study in groups to maximize their grades.
Educational outcomes depend solely on the method of studying used by students.
Individual study sessions can be as beneficial as group study sessions for all subjects.
Group study is beneficial, but it may not be the best approach for every student.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The choice suggests that group study is the only effective method, which makes it too strong compared to the original argument.

items.stimulus: In a recent study of urban park usage, researchers found that people who walked their dogs frequented parks more often than those who did not own dogs. Therefore, to increase the number of visitors to urban parks, cities should encourage dog ownership among residents.
items.question: Which of the following is a necessary assumption for the argument above to be valid?

choices.text: Encouraging dog ownership will lead to more people visiting parks regularly.
Most people prefer visiting parks without pets.
People who own dogs are more likely to exercise than those who do not.
Urban parks are attractive to dog owners because of their open spaces.
Dog ownership has no impact on an individual's likelihood to visit parks.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: This choice discusses preferences that may not relate to the argument's focus on encouraging dog ownership to increase park visits.

items.stimulus: The city council has proposed a new initiative to plant trees along all major roads to improve air quality. They argue that increasing green spaces will lead to a healthier urban environment and reduce the amount of air pollutants.
items.question: What principle underlies the city council's argument for the tree-planting initiative?

choices.text: Increasing green spaces in urban areas can lead to improved environmental conditions and public health.
Improving air quality is essential for the health of urban wildlife.
Planting trees in cities always leads to a decrease in air pollution levels.
Urban environments should prioritize aesthetics over environmental health.
All urban initiatives aimed at improving air quality must involve trees as a primary solution.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While improving air quality is important, the argument specifically addresses urban public health, making B irrelevant to the core issue at hand.

items.question: What is the flaw in the mayor's argument?

choices.text: The argument ignores other potential solutions for improving public safety, such as investing in mental health services or youth programs.

choices.text: Students who receive tutoring for more hours will likely see improved math scores.
Only students who struggle in math benefit from tutoring programs.
All students will benefit equally from after-school tutoring regardless of their previous performance.
Tutoring programs should be limited to students with the lowest math scores for maximum effectiveness.
The primary benefit of tutoring is to increase test scores in all subjects.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who use digital flashcards score higher on vocabulary tests compared to those who use traditional paper flashcards. Researchers suggest that the interactive nature of digital flashcards boosts engagement and retention of information.
items.question: Which of the following is most strongly supported by the study's findings?

choices.text: Using digital flashcards can improve vocabulary test scores for students.
Traditional paper flashcards are ineffective for all students.
All students should switch to digital flashcards for better learning outcomes.
Engagement and retention are not important factors in learning vocabulary.
Students who do not use flashcards may still perform well on vocabulary tests.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While B implies that traditional flashcards are completely ineffective, the study only indicates a comparative advantage for digital flashcards, not an absolute failure of traditional ones.

Community interactions are always beneficial for neighborhood safety.

Whether employee well-being should be prioritized over productivity.
Whether missed deadlines can affect employee morale.
Whether longer work hours lead to increased productivity.
Whether community meetings are effective for discussing workplace changes.

choices.text: Mandatory after-school tutoring programs will be effective for all students in improving math scores.
Students who attend after-school tutoring are naturally better at math than those who do not.
Higher math test scores lead to better overall academic performance for students.
Most students require tutoring to succeed in math.
After-school tutoring sessions are more productive than regular classroom instruction.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it suggests a relationship between tutoring and performance, it incorrectly assumes that attendance alone is the reason for the higher scores.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that people who regularly consume green tea tend to have lower cholesterol levels. Some health experts suggest that drinking green tea causes lower cholesterol. items.question: Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument that green tea consumption causes lower cholesterol levels?

choices.text: Many people with low cholesterol levels consume green tea as one of many healthful practices, but not all green tea drinkers have low cholesterol.
Drinking green tea has been linked to various other health benefits unrelated to cholesterol levels.
Researchers found that individuals who do not consume green tea have higher cholesterol levels in general.
Most health experts agree that a balanced diet is important for maintaining healthy cholesterol levels.
People who consume green tea often believe it helps improve their health.

items.question: What method of reasoning is being used in the argument?

choices.text: The argument wrongly assumes that two different activities have the same benefits based solely on their physical nature.
The argument compares two activities and concludes that one is superior based on their similarities in physical activity.
The argument uses a generalization about physical activity to assert a specific outcome for yoga.
The argument is based on anecdotal evidence from the influencer's own experience with yoga.
The argument suggests that because both yoga and weightlifting are forms of exercise, they have equal effects on all aspects of health.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The choice suggests that the argument's comparison is valid, whereas it actually misapplies the similarity in a way that overlooks relevant differences.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that dogs who are fed a high-protein diet exhibit increased energy levels compared to those fed a standard diet. Therefore, all dogs should be fed a high-protein diet to enhance their overall vitality.
items.question: Which of the following arguments contains a similar flaw in reasoning as the argument above?

choices.text: A survey showed that students who study late at night score higher on math tests than those who study in the morning. Thus, all students should study late at night to improve their grades.
Research shows that plants given more water grew taller than those given less; therefore, watering a plant more causes it to grow taller.
