A clinical trial found that patients who take vitamin D supplements recover from colds more quickly than those who don't. Thus, all patients should take vitamin D supplements during cold season.
A study found that people who walk regularly tend to weigh less than those who are sedentary. Hence, exercise is beneficial for weight management.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: D shares the leap from one study to a universal recommendation, but its recommended benefit is exactly the outcome measured (faster cold recovery); it lacks the stimulus's scope shift from a narrow measured effect (energy) to a broader claim (vitality), which A reproduces.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who study later in the evening tend to have higher GPAs than those who study in the morning. items.question: Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument that night studying may not actually cause higher GPAs?

items.stimulus: Last summer, the town of Maplewood implemented a new recycling program aimed at reducing landfill waste. items.question: What best explains the apparent contradiction between increased recycling rates and the continued rise in landfill waste?

choices.text: The increase in residents and businesses led to an overall increase in waste production, which outweighed the benefits of the recycling program.
Residents have started to recycle only certain materials, reducing the overall effectiveness of the recycling program.
The recycling program is not widely used by long-term residents, who continue to dispose of their waste in the landfill.
The town's landfill has reduced its capacity, making it appear that waste is increasing despite more recycling.
Many residents are incorrectly disposing of recyclable materials, leading to a greater amount of waste being sent to the landfill.

items.stimulus: A recent study showed that students who study late at night perform better on math tests than those who study in the morning. Therefore, students who want to improve their math test scores should consider studying late at night.

Students who study math in the evening typically have more free time than those who study in the morning.
Students who study in the morning perform poorly on all subjects, not just math.

It suggests that studying alone is ineffective for all students.
It implies that group study is the only way to improve academic performance.
It reinforces the idea that high exam scores are the most important measure of student success.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it may seem unrelated, the claim is directly tied to the argument's conclusion about encouraging group study.

items.stimulus: In a recent study, researchers found that students who studied late at night scored higher on math exams than those who studied in the morning. Therefore, studying late at night is the best approach for improving math scores.

All studies should be conducted at night for the best outcomes.

Consuming green tea is the only way to reduce stress levels effectively.
All beverages have an impact on stress levels.
Most people prefer drinking green tea over other beverages.
Lower stress levels contribute positively to overall health.

People visit coffee shops primarily for their milk options.

Non-pet owners are generally unhappy because they do not have pets.
Everyone who owns a pet reports lower anxiety and depression levels.

There is a growing trend of people prioritizing breakfast in their morning routines due to social media influences.

Eating breakfast is popular among students who are encouraged by teachers to maintain good study habits.
A majority of students surveyed claimed they feel better when they eat breakfast before school begins.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it's true that there may be a correlation between breakfast and math performance, it does not directly support the argument that eating breakfast causes improved performance.

A person exercises for 15 minutes a day and feels that sufficient for improving their mental health.

items.stimulus: In a recent study, it was found that coffee drinkers were more likely to report experiencing stress compared to non-coffee drinkers. However, the same study noted that coffee drinkers typically reported feeling more alert and productive than non-coffee drinkers.

choices.text: Coffee drinkers might experience stress due to the stimulating effects of caffeine, which also contributes to their feelings of alertness and productivity.

items.question: Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument that studying in groups causes higher test scores?

choices.text: Students who study in groups often form study schedules that keep them more accountable than when studying alone.

items.question: Which of the following can be inferred from the statements above?

choices.text: Students who participate in after-school tutoring for math are likely to improve their math test scores.
All students who attend any after-school program will perform better in all subjects.
Improvement in math scores is solely due to participation in after-school tutoring sessions.
After-school programs in subjects other than math enhance students' performance in math as well.
Tutoring in subjects other than math can lead to better performance in math tests.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The statement about after-school programs only applies to math and does not support a generalization about all subjects.

items.stimulus: In a recent survey, 75% of people reported enjoying classical music. However, our sales data shows that only 30% of customers who buy music purchases are for classical albums. Therefore, it is clear that most people who enjoy classical music do not actually buy it.
items.question: What is the flaw in the argument?

choices.text: The argument assumes that enjoyment of classical music should directly correlate with purchasing behavior, which is not necessarily the case.
The conclusion does not follow from the premises because it overlooks other potential reasons for low sales, such as availability or marketing issues.
The survey results about enjoyment of classical music are not relevant to the sales data provided, making the argument flawed.
The argument assumes that the 30% purchasing rate is definitive proof that the majority of classical music enthusiasts do not buy music.
The sales data is likely skewed by the popularity of other music genres, which implies that classical music could still be popular.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While B points out possible external factors affecting sales, it does not directly address the assumption about enjoyment and purchasing behavior.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that people who regularly consume green tea tend to have lower rates of heart disease than those who do not consume it. Therefore, drinking green tea causes a reduction in heart disease rates.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument that drinking green tea causes a reduction in heart disease rates?

choices.text: Many people who drink green tea also follow healthier diets and exercise regularly, both of which are known to lower heart disease risk.
Green tea has been shown to have numerous health benefits beyond heart health.
Heart disease rates have been declining in the general population over the last decade.
Some studies indicate that only specific types of green tea are beneficial for heart health.
People who drink green tea often believe it helps prevent heart disease, which may lead them to overlook other health factors.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While green tea's health benefits are mentioned, this choice does not address whether it specifically causes a reduction in heart disease rates.

items.stimulus: In recent studies, researchers found that people who consume more than five servings of fruits and vegetables a day report feeling significantly happier than those who eat fewer. items.question: What is the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.text: Increasing fruit and vegetable intake could lead to improved mental health outcomes.
People who eat more fruits and vegetables are generally happier than those who do not.
A diet rich in fruits and vegetables is beneficial for physical health.
Eating fruits and vegetables daily has no impact on one’s happiness levels.
Mental health outcomes are solely dependent on diet.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it is tempting to choose this as the conclusion, it focuses on happiness rather than implying a broader outcome related to mental health.

items.stimulus: In a recent survey of pet owners, 80% reported that having a pet improved their overall happiness. items.question: Which of the following can be inferred from the survey results?

choices.text: Pet ownership is associated with increased happiness and reduced stress.
All pet owners feel happier than those without pets.
Individuals who do not own pets are likely to be unhappy.
A majority of people believe that having a pet is essential for happiness.
Pets are the only factor that can improve a person's well-being.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: Although it might seem like all pet owners are happier, the survey only indicates a majority, not an absolute.

items.stimulus: In a recent study, researchers found that students who participated in after-school art programs scored higher in creativity than those who did not. Therefore, enrolling students in after-school art programs can significantly enhance their creative abilities.
items.question: What role does the claim about students scoring higher in creativity play in the argument?

choices.text: It provides evidence to support the conclusion that after-school art programs enhance creativity.
It introduces an unrelated topic about academic performance in general.
It contradicts the idea that art programs are beneficial for students.
It suggests that creativity is the only important skill for students to develop.
It implies that creativity can be measured through standardized tests.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: Choice B is incorrect because it misinterprets the relationship, mistakenly suggesting that the study's findings are unrelated to the argument about art programs.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who regularly participate in extracurricular activities tend to have higher grades than those who do not. The study suggests that being involved in activities outside of school may foster better time management skills and a stronger work ethic.
items.question: Which of the following is best supported by the statements above?

choices.text: Students involved in extracurricular activities are likely to perform better academically than those who are not.
All students who participate in extracurricular activities will have high grades regardless of other factors.
Time management skills and work ethic are the only reasons students have high grades.
Extracurricular activities are the most important factor in determining a student's academic success.
Students who do not participate in extracurricular activities cannot achieve high grades.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While students involved in extracurricular activities tend to have higher grades, the statement does not assert that all such students will achieve high grades without regard to other factors.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who study late at night score higher on math exams than those who study in the morning. Additionally, the study revealed that late-night studying tends to be more effective for students who are naturally night owls. items.question: Which conclusion is most strongly supported by the statements above?

choices.text: Students who are night owls might benefit from later school start times to improve their math exam scores.
All students perform better academically when they study at night.
Morning studying has no effect on math exam scores for any students.
Students should only study late at night to maximize their math scores.
Educators should consider individual student study habits when determining school schedules.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The statement about all students implies a universal truth that is not supported by the specifics of the study, which only focuses on night owls.

items.stimulus: During a recent study, it was found that students who consistently take notes during lectures score higher on exams compared to those who do not take notes. Therefore, taking notes is essential for academic success.
items.question: What is the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.text: Taking notes is essential for academic success.
Students who take notes tend to score higher than those who do not.
Higher exam scores indicate better academic performance overall.
Note-taking practices should be encouraged in all educational settings.
Most students prefer to take notes during lectures.

Based on this finding, health experts recommend that individuals experiencing mental health issues incorporate regular physical activity into their daily routines.
items.question: According to the principle outlined in the study, which of the following actions best aligns with the recommendation made by health experts?

choices.text: A person who feels anxious starts jogging three times a week to help manage their symptoms.
A person who enjoys reading decides to start exercising only occasionally, claiming it is more important to focus on their hobbies.
A person who exercises regularly but has not experienced any mental health issues continues their routine without change.
A person who feels overwhelmed by stress opts to try yoga once a month instead of consistent exercise.
A person begins a rigorous exercise program solely to improve their physical appearance, disregarding their mental health.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While focusing on hobbies is beneficial, the recommendation specifically urges regular exercise to improve mental health, making this choice irrelevant to the principle.

items.question: What flaw is present in the mayor's argument?

choices.text: The mayor ignores the possibility of other funding sources that could improve public transportation.
The mayor assumes that raising taxes would be universally unpopular among the citizens.

The mayor fails to consider the impacts of public transportation on the local economy.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: Although the mayor's conclusion could lead to unpopularity, it is not the main issue; the argument's flaw lies in presenting only two options.

items.stimulus: In a recent survey, 60% of respondents reported that they prefer coffee over tea. Therefore, coffee is the most popular beverage among the population as a whole.
items.question: Which of the following assumptions, if added to the argument, would guarantee that the conclusion is true?

choices.text: The survey respondents are representative of the overall population.
Most people drink coffee rather than tea.
Tea is less popular than coffee in every demographic group.
Respondents who prefer tea were less likely to respond to the survey.
The majority of the population does not drink any beverage at all.

Participants report that they enjoy the social aspects of attending group exercise classes.

items.stimulus: In a recent survey, 80% of participants reported that they felt more productive when working from home compared to working in the office. Therefore, employers should allow their employees to work from home to enhance overall productivity.
items.question: What role does the claim about the survey results play in the argument?

choices.text: It serves as evidence to support the conclusion that working from home boosts productivity.
It suggests that working in the office is detrimental to productivity.
It provides a general observation about workplace preferences among the surveyed participants.
It implies that productivity is the only factor employers should consider when deciding work arrangements.
It indicates that most employees prefer working from home over working in the office regardless of productivity.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While the claim discusses productivity, it does not imply that working in the office is bad; rather, it focuses on the benefits of working from home.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who study late at night score higher on math exams than those who study in the morning. Therefore, studying late at night causes better performance in math exams.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most seriously weaken the argument above?

choices.text: Many students who study late at night also participate in after-school tutoring programs that improve their math skills.
The majority of students prefer studying late at night over any other time.
Students who study in the morning generally report enjoying their study sessions.
Higher math scores are often correlated with a student's natural ability in mathematics rather than their study time.
Students who study at night tend to have less sleep, which may negatively affect their overall health.

choices.text: Towns with more public parks tend to have more organized community events throughout the year.
Some towns with fewer public parks still have high levels of community engagement due to active local organizations.
People generally prefer living in towns with green spaces and parks.
Communities that engage residents often invest in public infrastructure, including parks.
Public parks have been shown to reduce crime in communities, leading to safer environments.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it is true that some towns without parks may still engage the community, it does not strengthen the argument about the impact of parks on engagement.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who study late at night tend to have higher grades compared to those who study during the day. Therefore, studying late at night must be the reason for their better performance.
items.question: Which of the following, if true, would most strengthen the argument that studying late at night causes higher grades?

choices.text: Students who study late at night report feeling less distracted and more focused during their study sessions.
Many students also have other habits, such as exercising regularly, which contribute to their academic success.
The study did not track how much sleep students got after studying late at night.
Higher grades are often associated with students who engage in collaborative study sessions, which frequently occur during the day.
There is a growing trend of students preferring late-night study sessions over early morning ones.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: While it discusses factors related to student success, it does not address the direct link between studying late and higher grades.

items.stimulus: In a recent survey, 80% of participants reported that they regularly consume organic produce, yet sales data from local grocery stores show that organic produce accounts for only 30% of total produce sales.

choices.text: Many participants may buy organic produce from farmers' markets or other sources that are not included in grocery store sales data.
The survey may have included respondents who do not actually buy organic produce but believe they should be consuming it.
The survey indicates a preference for organic produce, which may not translate into actual purchasing habits.
Organic produce may be more expensive, leading many consumers to choose non-organic options despite their preference.
The grocery stores surveyed may not offer a wide variety of organic options, limiting consumer purchases.

items.question: What is the reasoning flaw in this argument?

choices.text: The argument assumes that what is true of the individual pieces must also be true of the whole box, which may not be the case.
The argument overlooks that some people might not like sweet candy, making the conclusion invalid for everyone.
The argument fails to consider that the box could contain a mix of sweet and sour candies, leading to an inaccurate conclusion.
The argument wrongly claims that since the pieces are sweet, someone must dislike them, which is irrelevant to the conclusion.
The argument assumes the box is made up of only sweet candies based on the assumption that people generally like sweet treats.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: This choice misinterprets the argument by focusing on individual preferences rather than addressing the actual flaw of assuming the group shares the same characteristic as its parts.

choices.text: The argument denies the antecedent by concluding that without free samples, a restaurant can still have high-quality food, which does not necessarily follow.

The argument presents a specific case to make a broad generalization about all restaurants, which can be misleading.

The argument relies on anecdotal evidence from customers rather than statistical data about restaurant quality, which weakens its conclusion.

items.stimulus: A recent study found that students who drink coffee tend to perform better on exams compared to those who do not. Therefore, drinking coffee must improve students' exam performance.

However, these benefits are often unevenly distributed, with marginalized neighborhoods lacking adequate access to such resources. Thus, while urban green spaces can contribute significantly to enhancing quality of life, their design and implementation must prioritize inclusivity and equitable access to serve all community members effectively.

items.passage: In recent years, the concept of cultural appropriation has garnered significant attention within academic and social discourse. Cultural appropriation refers to the adoption of elements from one culture by members of another culture, often without permission or understanding of the original context. Critics argue that this practice can perpetuate stereotypes and diminish the significance of cultural symbols. For example, the commercialization of Native American headdresses at music festivals raises concerns about disrespecting indigenous traditions. Proponents of cultural borrowing, however, contend that cultural exchange can foster understanding and appreciation among diverse groups. They argue that the blending of cultures has historically led to innovation and creativity, contributing to the richness of human expression. This juxtaposition of viewpoints illustrates a broader tension in contemporary society, where the lines between appreciation and appropriation are often blurred, necessitating a nuanced examination of the ethics surrounding cultural exchange.

As the conversation develops, it is clear that a balanced perspective is necessary, one that weighs both the benefits of technological advancements against their possible drawbacks. items.passage: In recent years, the concept of digital literacy has evolved significantly, reflecting the increasing influence of technology in everyday life. Originally defined as the ability to read and write in a digital context, it now encompasses a broader skill set, including the capacity to critically evaluate online information. This shift acknowledges the complexities of the digital landscape, where misinformation proliferates. For instance, studies show that individuals who are digitally literate are more adept at distinguishing credible sources from dubious ones, thereby enhancing their decision-making abilities in personal and professional settings. Furthermore, educational institutions are beginning to integrate digital literacy into curricula, understanding its importance in preparing students for a technology-driven world. This initiative not only aims to equip students with necessary skills but also seeks to cultivate a generation that actively engages with digital content rather than passively consuming it. items.passage: In the realm of modern literature, the significance of narrative voice cannot be overstated. Authors frequently employ various narrative perspectives to shape readers' experiences and influence their interpretations. For instance, a first-person narrative may evoke intimacy and immediacy, allowing readers to connect deeply with the protagonist's feelings. Conversely, a third-person omniscient voice can provide a broader context, revealing the thoughts and motivations of multiple characters. This manipulation of perspective can challenge readers' preconceived notions and prompt them to question the reliability of the narrator. Furthermore, the choice of narrative voice often reflects broader themes within the text, such as isolation, community, or the passage of time. By analyzing these voices, one can discern the underlying messages and emotional landscapes crafted by the author, ultimately enriching the reading experience. Thus, understanding narrative voice is critical not only for literary analysis but also for fostering empathy and understanding in a diverse society.

items.passage: In contemporary discussions surrounding urban development, the balance between preserving cultural heritage and fostering economic growth has sparked considerable debate. Advocates for preservation argue that historical sites encapsulate the identity of a community and contribute significantly to its social fabric. They assert that erasing these landmarks in favor of modern constructions not only diminishes the aesthetic value of urban spaces but also risks alienating residents who derive a sense of belonging from their surroundings. Conversely, proponents of economic growth maintain that new developments are essential for attracting investment and improving infrastructure. They contend that revitalizing urban spaces can lead to increased job opportunities and a more vibrant local economy. While the tension between these two perspectives is palpable, it is crucial to find a middle ground that honors the past while embracing the future. A pragmatic approach, which could include integrating historical elements into new designs, may serve to satisfy both camps, fostering a sense of community while still allowing for necessary growth.

items.passage: The phenomenon of social media has engendered a profound transformation in the landscape of communication. items.passage: In the realm of urban development, the debate surrounding high-density housing often centers on the balance between community benefits and individual privacy. items.passage: In contemporary discussions surrounding the ethics of artificial intelligence (AI), a pivotal concern arises regarding the responsibility of creators when their technologies lead to unintended consequences. Particularly in sectors such as healthcare and law enforcement, AI systems often operate on algorithms that may inadvertently perpetuate biases present in the training data. This issue is compounded by the opacity of many AI systems, which can obscure the decision-making processes from scrutiny. The author posits that the ethical framework guiding AI development must evolve to account for these potential pitfalls. By emphasizing accountability, creators can design systems that not only adhere to legal standards but also promote ethical implications in their deployment. The author further illustrates this point by referencing case studies where biased AI outcomes have sparked public outcry and regulatory debates. Ultimately, the passage advocates for a proactive approach to AI ethics, one that requires intensive collaboration between technologists, ethicists, and policymakers to ensure that advancements in AI benefit society as a whole rather than exacerbate existing inequalities.

items.passage: The rise of digital media has significantly influenced contemporary art, altering not only techniques of creation but also methods of distribution and consumption. Artists today increasingly embrace technology, using digital tools to produce works that challenge traditional notions of authorship and originality. items.passage: The emergence of global capitalism has transformed traditional agricultural practices in many developing countries. As markets have opened, smallholder farmers are increasingly faced with the challenge of adapting to the demands of international trade. In particular, the shift towards cash crops has resulted in both economic opportunities and social upheaval. While some farmers benefit financially from exporting their goods, others find themselves at a disadvantage, struggling to compete with larger agribusinesses that dominate the market. This tension raises important questions about sustainability and food security, as land that once supported diverse subsistence farming is now being repurposed for monoculture. Critics argue that this shift undermines local food systems, exacerbating poverty for those who cannot adapt. Thus, the paradox of global capitalism is evident: while it seeks to promote growth and efficiency, it often does so at the expense of local communities and traditional ways of life.

Global capitalism has no effect on local food systems.

two_answer_fork.why_runner_up_wrong: The passage acknowledges that while some larger agribusinesses benefit, it does not state that only they benefit.
